<!-- FORGE:INVESTIGATOR -->
## Investigation Report

### Verdict/Confidence/Severity/Task Type

| Field | Finding |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Confirmed recovery/projection gap on the parent-dispatch merge path; direct ordering is already early but lacks this focused recovery assertion |
| Confidence | High |
| Severity | Medium / P2 |
| Task Type | Focused workflow correctness fix with regression coverage |

### What Was Claimed

After GitHub records a successful merge, post-merge artifact, issue-close, cleanup, or terminal-work failures can prevent the merged workflow label from being projected. A durable merge can therefore remain shown as `workflow:awaiting-merge`.

### What We Found

The current base contains two merge implementations. Direct finalization records the merge effect and `merge` phase completion, then calls `#projectWorkflowStage(link, "merged", ...)` before `postReviewCompletionArtifacts`, close, cleanup, and terminal artifacts. The parent dispatcher merge node likewise records its merge effect and attempts the merged projection before post-merge artifacts, but its durable state is represented by a still-running `merge` node until the later node-completion append.

On restart/reconciliation, `#reconcileWorkflowProjection` handles a completed run or a completed merge phase as merged. However, when the parent merge node is still running after its merge effect was durably recorded, reconciliation derives `workflow:awaiting-merge` from `workflowStageForNodeTransition("merge", "started")` and does not inspect the durable merge effect. A post-merge exception therefore leaves the issue projected as awaiting merge until another unrelated terminal state transition, and may never retry the merged projection.

### Root Cause

Projection recovery is driven by the latest node status instead of the strongest durable merge evidence. A recorded `effectType: "merge"` is authoritative evidence that the external merge succeeded, but the reconciliation decision does not prioritize that evidence over an incomplete parent merge node.

### Affected Files

| Path | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| `src/workflows/work-on.ts` | Prioritize durable merge-effect evidence during workflow-label reconciliation. |
| `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` | Add focused regression coverage for a durable merge effect with a still-running merge node. |

### Evidence

- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` parent merge path calls `mergePullRequest`, appends `effect.recorded` with `effectType: "merge"`, then attempts the merged projection before `postReviewCompletionArtifacts`.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` reconciliation currently maps a latest running `merge` node to `workflow:awaiting-merge` and only uses `phase.merge` when there is no latest node.
- `src/core/state.ts` persists recorded effects independently from node completion, so a merge effect remains available after a post-merge interruption.
- `test/adapters/github-projection.test.ts` verifies label replacement/idempotency but does not model a restart between durable merge effect and parent node completion.

### History Findings

The supplied issue identifies PR `#117` and finding `workflow-correctness-001`. The assigned frozen base has no local diff and retains both direct and parent-dispatch merge paths; the relevant durable-effect/reconciliation distinction is present in the current source. No additional repository-local history artifact was provided for this run.

### Recommendation

Add a small pure stage-selection helper used by `#reconcileWorkflowProjection` that returns `merged` whenever authoritative merge-effect evidence exists, before evaluating terminal status or latest node status. Keep the existing immediate pre-post-merge projection calls. Add a regression test proving a running parent merge node with a recorded merge effect selects `merged`, while a merge node without that effect still selects `awaitingMerge`.

### Related Issues

- Source review finding: PR `#117`, finding `workflow-correctness-001`.
- Source issue referenced by the finding: `#92`.
- Remediation issue: `#119`.

### Decomposition Assessment

Single bounded correctness concern. No decomposition is warranted.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Reproduce/validate the interrupted parent-merge reconciliation state.
- [ ] Treat a durable merge effect as authoritative for the merged workflow projection.
- [ ] Preserve awaiting-merge projection when no durable merge effect exists.
- [ ] Add focused regression coverage and run the required named verification.
- [ ] Re-review the exact implementation head.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT -->
## Builder Contract

### Objective

Ensure workflow-label reconciliation projects `workflow:merged` whenever the authoritative run state contains a durable merge effect, even if post-merge work interrupted the parent merge node before node completion.

### Allowed Paths

- `src/workflows/work-on.ts`
- `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts`

### Forbidden Changes

- Do not change GitHub merge, close, cleanup, push, or label API authority.
- Do not change `.forge/config.json`, review policy, branch policy, event schemas, or state reducer semantics.
- Do not reorder or bypass required post-merge artifacts, issue closure, cleanup, CI, or review gates.
- Do not add credentials, fixtures containing production/private data, or unrelated refactors.
- Do not modify files outside the two allowed paths.

### Invariants

- A merge effect is considered durable only after it is recorded in the authoritative run state.
- Existing immediate merged-label projection remains before post-merge work.
- Without durable merge evidence, a running merge node continues to project `workflow:awaiting-merge`.
- Reconciliation remains idempotent and safe to retry.
- All existing workflow labels, terminal recovery, review, and merge authority behavior remain unchanged.

### Deliverables

- A pure stage-selection helper that recognizes recorded merge effects before latest-node fallback.
- `#reconcileWorkflowProjection` wired to use that helper.
- Focused regression tests for durable merge evidence and the awaiting-merge control case.

### Acceptance Mapping

| Check | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Validate the finding | Trace and encode the interrupted parent merge state: merge node still running, merge effect already recorded. |
| Fix root cause | Prioritize durable `effectType: "merge"` evidence during reconciliation. |
| Regression coverage | Add assertions for merged projection with durable effect and awaiting projection without it. |
| Required verification | Run named `check` through `forge_verify`; parent owns GitHub CI acceptance. |
| Exact-head review | Prepare the bound PR and launch fresh correctness/security reviewers against its frozen head. |

### Out of Scope

- Product behavior beyond workflow-label projection.
- New GitHub endpoints or durable event types.
- Changes to direct merge finalization ordering, which already projects merged before post-merge work.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

### Relevant History

- Issue `#119` remediates review finding `workflow-correctness-001` from PR `#117` and source issue `#92`.
- The frozen base contains direct and parent-dispatch merge implementations.
- Parent-dispatch state records the merge effect before completing the merge node, creating the restart window described by the finding.

### Callers and Data Flow

- Parent merge execution calls GitHub merge, records `effectType: "merge"`, and starts post-merge artifact work.
- `#reconcileWorkflowProjection` runs during attach/restart and calls `#projectWorkflowStage` to replace the workflow label.
- The latest parent merge node is `running` until its later `node.completed` event; current fallback therefore yields awaiting merge.
- Authoritative `RunState.effects` survives the interruption and is the correct recovery signal.

### CI Surface

- `.forge/config.json` configures required named check `check` as `npm run check`.
- The check runs TypeScript typechecking and the full Node test suite.
- GitHub CI is required for `staging` and remains parent-owned after PR preparation.

### Prior Findings

- The cited finding states that post-merge exceptions can prevent the later merged label projection.
- Existing tests cover workflow-label mapping and projector idempotency, but not reconciliation from a durable merge effect while the parent merge node remains incomplete.

### Hazards

- Treating arbitrary effects as merge evidence could project a false terminal state; restrict the helper to `effectType === "merge"`.
- A no-effect running merge must remain awaiting merge so merge authority cannot be inferred prematurely.
- The change must not make a merge effect itself complete close/cleanup or bypass durable state transitions.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Implementation Plan

1. Add an exported pure helper that returns the `merged` workflow stage when `RunState.effects` contains a recorded merge effect; otherwise return no override. (finding-validation)
2. Call the helper first in `#reconcileWorkflowProjection`, before completed-run, phase, and latest-node fallbacks. (root-cause-fix)
3. Add a focused test showing a `running` merge node plus a recorded merge effect selects `merged`, and a running merge node without that effect remains `awaitingMerge`. (regression)
4. Inspect the assigned diff and run the required named `check` verification. (verification)
5. Commit the implementation, prepare the bound PR, and submit the exact frozen head to fresh correctness and security reviewers. (review)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Durable merge evidence wins over an incomplete parent merge node during projection reconciliation.
- [ ] No durable merge evidence preserves `workflow:awaiting-merge` behavior.
- [ ] Focused regression coverage passes.
- [ ] The actual changed-file set stays within the builder contract.
- [ ] Named verification passes and the exact implementation head is freshly reviewed.

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT:COMPLETE -->
